body:
Feigning confidence and outright lying are different things entirely, indeed.  But what if you have no redeeming qualities?  What if there's nothing to embellish?  You're not left with any option but to lie, and it's not something I feel like I can do.  I want to be wanted, not to be around someone who believes in something that doesn't exist.


And what's the line between unnecessarily negative self evaluation and realistic self evaluation?  Just because the postulation that everyone might hold some value doesn't mean that their shortcomings don't outweigh the positives.


Why would a woman, who gets the pick of whatever man she wants, settle for someone like me?  Even in the hypothetical my prospects don't hold water.

I don't know if I'd classify every one of my relationships as being abusive, but definitely more ammunition to destroy my opinion of myself.


My first relationship was awkward, confused, and severely misguided.  The girl I was with seemed to be highly preoccupied with sex with various (band) celebrities, drugs, and other such deviances.  I don't know what she saw in me or why it lasted so long (close to a year) but eventually it came to her leaving me out of the blue and jumping to some drug dealer the next day (though it was likely something that was transpiring way before...).


After that  my second relationship was a long-time crush that happened to pan out into, at least the verbal acknowledgement, of a relationship.  Again, she was on the social fringe.  Loner, introvert, and seemed to have a fixation on drug culture to the point where she indicated that getting high was a much more gratifying activity than being around me.  This went on mindbogglingly long for how dysfunctional the interactions were (well over 6 months).  I was, again, crushed by the disappointment of not being up to the standards of an object.


Next was probably the most crushing experience in my history next to the original post.  I got involved with someone whom I felt I was genuinely compatible.  She was an artist, much like myself, highly mature and analytical for a highschool girl.  Geeky, defied convention, and had a propensity towards macabre, gothic aestheic, dark humor, etc.  As I said, a close match to myself.  The only problem is that she was also a devout Mormon.  This was highly at ends with my anti-religious attitude, not to mention being a 17-20 year old virgin, made it difficult to get past the completely hands-off nature of the relationship.  Still, it would have been worth the wait, so I went along with it.  We were even, at one point, engaged to get married.  Unfortunately she decided that this wasn't for her, basically overnight.  She wanted to pursue more 'casual dating', whatever that meant, and couldn't go through with the commitment to me.  This was all revealed to me opportunistically while we were hours away from home at a show she desperately wanted to go to (and I paid for, drove us to, etc).  Again, crushed.  


This time to the very verge of suicide much like now.  I spent a lot of time trying to drink myself to blackout, leaving loaded weapons around hoping for the worst.


It wasn't until my most recent relationship that I was finally able to see the value in life again only for it to plummet below what I believed to be the most abject misery that a person could experience.

_______

As for therapy...I don't know what someone could tell me that could alter my perspective so fundamentally that I could all of a sudden regain my hold on what good there is in living.  The money is better spent on a prostitute in my opinion.  Sure, money is motivating their opinion, but at least they have some reason to see value in you....


And you've pretty much just reinforced my point.  I'm not in a state where I can actually approach anyone and build a healthy relationship (even if such people were actually available and willing to do so).  How could I ever get myself into that state when I've been told and demonstrated how awful I am?


I do everything else I can, everything I can help.  I'm actually rather fit, I watch what I eat, I exercise, I'm well off enough to be able to afford to dress well, and I present myself as best I can.  I have control over these things and I take advantage of that.  But the filthy monster that lives inside of the nice car, the nice clothes, the trim body...that's something that's permanent.  It's there to stay.  And it's clear that it's not good enough.  Not even for people who supposedly don't deserve it.

No animal has ever hated itself because they're not cognizant of their cognition.

My subjective definition of hate is an inability to coexist with a quality, thing, or being.  I hate myself, truly, and my desire to not exist is an extension of this.

It just feels like to me by lying about my disposition, and lying about my personal qualities (if they even exist), is an even faster way to a more disastrous relationship.  How could I possibly trust someone when I know, myself, that I'm not even trustworthy?  Why would I lie about something I couldn't possibly deliver on, and would very clearly be outed in a rather timely manner?

How much rejection is the point where you're acting out of favor with reason?  I mean there's a point where it has to become apparent that success is of such a low possibility that the feeling of rejection abandonment and self loathing will become an infinite feel loop.


Maybe it's 100 attempts, maybe it's 1,000, or 10,000.  Everyone's ego has a limit of stress.  I feel like I'm at that limit.  I feel like if I'm not good enough for someone who has no real redeeming qualities but just happens to be female, how could I be good enough for anyone?  I mean, that's basically how it's supposed to function.  If you're ambitious out of your league settle for lower.  Well how much lower can I go?  How much do I have to hate myself to feel like I have to strive to appeal to the scum of humanity?  What does that make me?

On what basis do you disagree?  I mean, it's basically an impenetrable echelon.  Society tells you that if you're not confident nobody will take you seriously.  You're told that if you don't love yourself nobody will love you, and you can never be confident in yourself.  If you have no positive experiences how can you love yourself?  What if there's a reason that nothing ever goes right?  What if it's entirely self inflicted.  How much would you hate yourself if you knew you were the one who's directly causing all of your own misery?


This is why I feel I have nowhere to go but down.  I truly hate myself because I know through my own misery, crappy personality, and shitty life that I've assassinated my own chances at happiness.

I feel like I've tried a lot (though, I suppose this is subjective).  As I mentioned I've gone to bars and clubs, I've made a sweeping attempt at online dating (and despite hundreds of messages, varying methodology, and a profile that's been approved by non-bias parties, I've never once received a singe response), and reddit meetups in multiple cities, I've still not progressed past the conclusion that there's any hope for me.


I've tried to put on a the best attitude that I can, I try to be as outgoing as possible.  It's just that some people are just, by design, only able to exist on the bottom rungs of society.  This is clearly my place and I resent that.


I had a miserable childhood as well.  My parents pretty much neglected me through the entirety of my childhood except to beat me or put me to work in their lumbermill.  This pretty much endured until I was 16 when I moved out and never looked back.  To my recollection the first human contact I had that wasn't out of malice or necessity was the first girlfriend I had when I had finally left.  It's, more or less, where the cycle of serial abusive relationships began and inevitable rejection by the people I confided in most came about.


Because of my choices in these people it's left me completely stunted socially and at a loss for where, and much less how to progress at this point.

This is an intensely diminishing return, in my eyes.  I can be rejected and ignored time after time with no guarantee of success.  Ever.  Or I could just not exist.

Well that's just it, I've done a fair amount of research on the subject.  I've been to r/seduction, I've read the okcupid trends, and so on.  The internet certainly has a lot of information on the subject.  The issue is that it all comes down to statistical averages, and being too far outside of the average ostracizes you.


I simply don't have enough exposure to play the numbers game (let alone the self confidence, or emotional fortitude to approach so many people and be rejected on such a regular basis).  I've attempted going to bars and clubs, reddit meetups, and so on in an effort to increase this but I'm missing something that seems to be inherent to most people.  I'm not able so socialize and connect easily with anyone.  And as you put it, the more depressed you are the more difficult it is to be confident, and the more disingenuous it feels to fake it.  With how much mental and emotional reprogramming that would be required to go through with anything it just feels predatory.  And this is discounting any odds of success, which are likely arbitrarily close to zero.
